submitted.rationale: Index 22 (Cu0.17 Sb0.83) had the highest EQE of the three measured: 0.00456%. Index 16, near stoichiometric CuSb2O6, gave 0.00385%, and the Cu-rich index 5 was negative. The Sb-rich film (probably CuSb2O6 + Sb2O4, with a 1.67 eV MEGNet gap for Sb2O4) gave a slightly higher photoresponse at 2.1 eV.

rejected.reason: EQE 0.00385%, slightly below index 22. MACE puts CuSb2O6 on the hull, but its photoresponse was weak.
Negative EQE (-0.0145%). MACE puts Cu2SbO5 1.16 eV/atom above the hull, so the film is probably CuO-rich with no anodic photoresponse.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts CuSb2O6 (trirutile) on the hull (0.0001 eV/atom), so index 16 (Sb 0.687, close to the 1:2 ratio) should be mostly single-phase CuSb2O6. MEGNet's 0.02 eV HSE gap is not credible for a Cu2+ d9 oxide; CuSb2O6 is a known visible-light photoanode, so this prediction doesn't count against it.

Mixed. MACE puts Cu2SbO5 1.16 eV/atom above the hull, so index 5 probably won't form that phase and will be CuO + CuSb2O6 instead. MEGNet gives Cu3Sb4O12 a 0.5 eV gap, which is uninformative. CuSb2O6 was weak at index 16, so I'm checking the Cu-rich side, where a CuO/CuSb2O6 heterojunction or a Cu-Sb oxide with a ~2.1 eV gap might absorb better at 2.1 eV.

Mild support. MEGNet gives Sb2O4 (mp-1819) a 1.67 eV HSE gap, below the 2.1 eV photon energy. So Sb-rich films (CuSb2O6 + Sb2O4) could add absorption and a heterojunction. The Sb-rich end is also the unexplored side, where the GP puts its highest UCB.
